name: Regimen EE-4A: Vincristine + Dactinomycin (Stage I-II Favorable Histology Wilms Tumor)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS Reference Regimen: COG NWTS-5 / AREN0532 Protocol

supportiveCare: Bowel management: stool softener (polyethylene glycol or lactulose) to prevent vincristine-induced constipation / paralytic ileus.
Hepatotoxicity monitoring: monitor for sinusoidal obstruction syndrome / veno-occlusive disease (SOS/VOD) associated with dactinomycin.
monitoring: CBC with differential and CMP before each cycle
Liver enzymes and total bilirubin (check for dactinomycin-induced hepatotoxicity)
Weekly neurological exam for peripheral motor/sensory neuropathy, loss of deep tendon reflexes, or abdominal distension

doseModificationRules.condition: Severe peripheral neuropathy (severe weakness, foot drop, or severe ileus)
doseModificationRules.text: Withhold vincristine until symptom resolution. Resume at 50% dose or discontinue if Grade >= 3 per physician discretion.

doseModificationRules.condition: Veno-occlusive disease / Hepatopathy (Bilirubin > 3x ULN or ALT > 5x ULN)
doseModificationRules.text: Hold dactinomycin until complete clinical and biochemical recovery. Resume with 50% dose reduction.

drugs.name: Vincristine
drugs.notes: Vincristine 1.5 mg/m2 IV push Day 1 (capped at absolute maximum 2.0 mg). In patients <= 12 kg or age < 1 year, dose is 0.05 mg/kg. Grounded in NWTS-5 / COG EE-4A protocol.

drugs.name: Dactinomycin (Actinomycin D)
drugs.notes: Dactinomycin 45 mcg/kg IV push Day 1 every 21 days (maximum single dose 2.3 mg). Alternatively 1.35 mg/m2 in older children (> 12 kg). NWTS-5 / COG EE-4A protocol standard.
